findings.claim: The wait's gh call has no actions scope and its error is discarded, so a denied call reads as 'no store job for this commit' and the wait never waits.
findings.evidence: The build job's permissions are contents: read and pages: read only (lines 48-50). A job-level permissions block sets every unlisted scope to none, so actions is none. GitHub's REST reference for the workflow-run endpoints says GitHub Apps must have actions:read, and GITHUB_TOKEN is an installation token (this is the documented model; not reproduced against GitHub from this sandbox). Line 106 ends with 2>/dev/null || echo "", and line 108 maps the empty string to 'no store job for this commit'. Reproduction: the run block was extracted with PyYAML and run under bash -e with a gh stub that prints 'HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by integration' to stderr and exits 1. Result: stdout 'no store job for this commit', exit 0, 1 gh call, 0 sleeps (scratch: run_scenarios.sh). The same query with this sandbox's own credentials works on the real repo: --commit of claude/hail-b3 prints 'completed success', and --commit of main's head prints 'null null'. Prediction to check: hail-store-b1.tar.gz does not exist yet (its URL returns 404), so if the wait is a no-op, this branch's first preview will likely fail with hail_history in the failed list; later pushes would pass silently on the previous asset. Fix: add actions: read to the build job's permissions, and remove 2>/dev/null or fail the step on a gh error.

findings.claim: The public release still serves hail-store.tar.gz, which holds the address stage's data. The rename stops main reading it, but nothing removes it, and DECISIONS still gates that stage.
findings.evidence: The release tagged hail-store lists one asset: hail-store.tar.gz, 72,068,928 bytes, updated 2026-10-20T02:22:42Z by the publish step of claude/hail-b3's store run 39355361340. An unauthenticated GET of its URL returns 206 (the repo is public). Reading member headers only, without extraction: 4,211 hail/a/r*.json shards in format hail-addresses-v1 hold 105,403 address points (street addresses and coordinates, for example '300 Lower River Road'), plus per-town hail/a/idx/<town>/ address indexes and hail/b building outlines. DECISIONS.md line 670 says B3 adds a dot for each address in the MSL Structures and Addresses Framework. Lines 735 and 741 say the MSL clause and MCA 2-6-1017 still gate the address stage. The B1 builder writes hail/index.json (hail.py line 1523), shards under hail/t/ (line 1479) and hail/manifest.json (line 1534), so the new name carries no address data. The old archive is also 31,129 hail/ files and 357.3 MiB unpacked, over the reader's limits (hail.py lines 750-751), which is why the rename exists. Owner decision: delete the old asset once main reads the new name, and keep any stage with open gates from uploading to the public release.

findings.claim: The comment says --require-live reports a stale asset, but the hail source is marked ok whenever the store loads, so a store days old passes the preview check.
findings.evidence: build.py line 257 records ok=True for any loaded store. hail.py line 376 sets only a page word when as_of is more than STALE_DAYS (3, line 82) old. build.py lines 675-676 test only the ok flag. Reproduction (a copy of the worktree in scratch; sample build with the fixture store, whose as_of is 2026-10-15): with --require-live and --now 2026-10-16T13:00:00Z the build exits 0; with --now 2026-10-26T13:00:00Z, eleven days later, it still exits 0 with hail_history ok=True, and the stale line appears on the Billings town page. Control: a missing store path exits 1 with 'Sources that failed or were stale: hail_history'. So a preview that reads yesterday's asset passes, and the only sign is the as_of date in the job summary. Fix: fail the hail source when as_of is older than the expected lag, or pass the expected as_of to the check; and correct this comment and the header at lines 7-8.

findings.claim: The wait treats any completed conclusion as finished, so a failed, cancelled or timed-out store run lets the preview build from the previous asset.
findings.evidence: Stub reproduction: 'completed failure' gives 'store job: completed failure, after 1 checks', exit 0, and the build step runs; 'completed cancelled' behaves the same. The publish is the store job's last step (hail-store.yml lines 68-76), so a failed run leaves the old asset in place, as the workflow header says (lines 5-6). Concurrency is group hail-store with cancel-in-progress false (hail-store.yml lines 28-29). GitHub's documented concurrency behaviour is that a newer queued run replaces an older pending one, which this wait would see as 'completed cancelled'. That was not observed here: the repo's four store runs include no cancelled run, so this part rests on the documentation. A store job that reaches its 60-minute timeout ends timed_out and takes the same path. Fix: break only on 'completed success'; for anything else, print the conclusion and fail the preview.

findings.claim: Every claude/** and codex/** branch's store job overwrites the shared public asset, so a later stage keeps main's file safe only by following a naming convention, and the old name was already overwritten by a branch.
findings.evidence: The push trigger covers claude/** and codex/** (line 18), and the upload (line 76) has no ref condition. The current asset was last written by claude/hail-b3's store run 39355361340 (2026-10-20 02:22). The comments at lines 15-16 and the DECISIONS amendment under D34 say a later stage names its own asset, but no test pins a stage's name: tests/test_hail.py asserts only the B1 names (lines 824 and 1668-1669). A later branch that keeps hail-store-b1.tar.gz would overwrite main's file, and its own tests would still pass. Fix: a per-stage asset constant checked against the URL in a test, and no public upload from a branch whose stage is not the one main reads.

findings.claim: The build job's timeout went from 15 to 60 minutes for every run, including main, which runs one build at a time, so a hung main run can hold back the public site for up to an hour.
findings.evidence: Only branch runs wait (line 97). A branch run measured 1.5 to 2.5 minutes before the wait (checkout, install, tests), about 1 minute of build and about 3 minutes of browser checks, so a 40-minute wait needs about 47 minutes in total, which is where the 60 comes from. Main's build job needs about 1.5 minutes (run 39663732785: job 19:40:50 to 19:42:14 UTC on 2026-10-21). Main's concurrency group (lines 40-42, cancel-in-progress false) runs one main build at a time, so a stuck main run delays the next deploy until its timeout, now 60 minutes instead of 15 (origin/main line 46). Fix: keep 15 for main, for example with a separate branch job or a ref-dependent expression. The expression form was not checked here; the YAML parse does not validate it.

findings.claim: The new wait step is covered only by string matches, so the defects above (silent denial, failed conclusions, the loop exit) pass the suite.
findings.evidence: The added assertions (lines 1844-1847) check text only: the if condition, the gh arguments, and 'timeout-minutes: 60', which the build job's line satisfies. Nothing checks the build job's actions permission, the conclusion handling or the loop bound. The stub runs reproduce each case, and the unit suite does not. AGENTS.md says to add or update tests with every behaviour change. Fix: a test that extracts the step's run block and runs it under bash -e with stub gh and sleep (as in the scratch harness), asserting that a denied call fails, that only 'completed success' ends the wait, and the 40-check bound; plus a YAML assertion that the build job's permissions include actions: read.

findings.claim: On the first main builds after the merge, the new asset URL returns 404 until the main store job publishes it, so the public hail page says it is unavailable for about 11 minutes.
findings.evidence: The URL .../releases/download/hail-store/hail-store-b1.tar.gz returned 404 at review time (curl -I -L). The store job runs on the merge push because its paths include website/hail.py and the workflow file. The measured B1 store run took 10.6 minutes (run 39133848230, job 13:57:50 to 14:08:29 UTC). The page then reads 'Hail history is unavailable: the history download failed: not published (HTTP 404). This is not the same as no hail.' This is the designed degradation, not a failure. Pushing the branch and waiting for its store job before merging avoids it.

findings.claim: The job summary labels the hail lines 'branch preview' on main too.
findings.evidence: build.py line 588 fills content['hail'] whenever --hail-history is set, and main now passes it (line 127). The summary step runs with always() on every run (line 142) and prints the header at line 169 whenever the key exists. Fix: name the build in the label, not the branch.

findings.claim: After 40 checks the wait ends with no message, so the last log line still reads 'waiting a minute' and the build goes on as if the store had finished.
findings.evidence: Stub run with 40 in-progress answers: exit 0, 40 gh calls, 40 sleeps, and final stdout line 'store job: in_progress ; waiting a minute'. The 'after N checks' line prints only on a break. Fix: echo a 'gave up after 40 checks' line after the loop.

findings.claim: The comment says a failed download reads 'Data unavailable', but the page says 'Hail history is unavailable: ... This is not the same as no hail.'
findings.evidence: The words are at website/hail.py line 163. A sample build with a missing store path (--hail-history --hail-store /nonexistent/x.tar.gz, without --require-live) exits 0, and the town page reads 'Hail history is unavailable: the history store file x.tar.gz is missing. This is not the same as no hail.' AGENTS.md rule 5 gives 'Data unavailable' as the missing-input wording, so either the comment or the copy should change.

findings.claim: An error outside the caught types would fail the main build and skip the deploy, and this diff adds that path to main.
findings.evidence: Collector.hail catches HailStoreError, OSError, ValueError, KeyError and TypeError (line 258). The Package step (website.yml line 200) and the deploy job (needs: build) run only when the build step succeeds. Missing-store and archive errors were tested and exit 0. No reachable uncaught type was found: verify runs before publish, and the B1 preview read a real store with --hail-history (run 39136078421, success). Residual risk is low.

findings.claim: Every main deploy now carries the store's hail/ tree, and its size is not recorded anywhere in the repo, so the Pages artifact size is unknown.
findings.evidence: The build copies the store's hail/ into _site (build.py _copy_hail, line 493), and the Package step uploads _site on every run. ROADMAP records the store's size as pending. The B3 archive unpacks to 357.3 MiB (measured). This review could not check GitHub Pages' size limits, and no failure has been seen.

result.notes:
Scope: read-only review of the uncommitted diff in /home/user/hail-b1/wt (branch claude/hail-b1, HEAD 7aec754) against origin/main e503a39, with the CI and shell lens. Every hunk and both workflow files were read in full.

Checks run: both workflow files parse with yaml.safe_load (both OK). The website unit line was run in a copy of the worktree (scratch tree/): 548 tests, 4 skipped, OK, exit 0. Failure path: a sample build with a missing store path and no --require-live exits 0 and records hail_history ok=False. The dash and name scan of the 59 added lines found no em or en dashes and no AI or model names. Real-repo reads used gh 2.89.0 and jq 1.7, which may differ from the runner's versions.

Not verified: the GitHub-side token outcome (finding 1), the concurrency replacement (finding 4), a ref-dependent expression in timeout-minutes (finding 5), and GitHub Pages size limits (last finding). The worktree was only read, with no edits, staging, commits or pushes.

Scratch folder: /home/user/hail-b1/out/review-live/claude-reviewer-ci/ holds the stub harness (wait_step.sh, run_scenarios.sh, run_bounds.sh), header-only archive readers (count_members.py, list_names.py, peek_members.py, count_addresses.py), dl/hail-store.tar.gz (the downloaded old asset, untrusted and never extracted), tree/ (the worktree copy used for the test and build runs), and unittest-*.txt logs.

findings.claim: The public hail-store release already serves a 357 MiB store with address and building folders. The diff leaves it in place, and the release notes describe the asset as radar estimates only.
findings.evidence: gh api repos/carson14dy/RoofingApp/releases/tags/hail-store lists one asset, hail-store.tar.gz (72,068,928 bytes, updated 2026-10-20T02:22:42Z). Its body says 'Radar estimates (NOAA MRMS MESH) for the five years... One asset, rebuilt daily... Radar estimates, not measurements or inspections.' An unauthenticated curl of its browser_download_url returned the file (sha256 745693528b289e8780c3f11192c2b657d1736dfe058086acabd027ee185cb3c8; copy in /home/user/hail-b1/out/review-live/reviewer/asset/). Tar listing, no extraction: 31,571 members, 31,129 regular files, 374,621,015 bytes (357.3 MiB). Folders: hail/a 11,714 files (the manifest lists hail/a/idx/<town>/<letter>.json), hail/b 5,615, hail/r 4,427, hail/j 4,598, hail/t 4,597, hail/s 60, hail/z 115, plus counts.json. This branch's code writes only hail/t/, index.json and manifest.json (website/hail.py:630-641, 1479, 1523-1534). The first commit that writes hail/a/idx is 1e32779 (2026-10-20T01:47:05Z, 'Hail history B3: ... one dot per building outline with its addresses, the typed-address search ... behind --hail-addresses (D36)'), on claude/hail-b3 (also in claude/hail-b5 and b5p). The release asset was updated about 35 minutes later, consistent with a branch store job publishing under the shared name. DECISIONS.md:669-670 says B3 adds 'a dot for each address in the Montana State Library (MSL) Structures and Addresses Framework (674,715 points)', and DECISIONS.md:735 and :741 tie the MSL clause and MCA 2-6-1017 to the address stage and to counsel. The rename does not stop branch store jobs from publishing address-level stores to this public release (hail-store.yml:17-18 push trigger; :65-76 publish). The D34 amendment does not mention the public asset. Owner action before go-live: decide whether to delete hail-store.tar.gz (gh release delete-asset hail-store hail-store.tar.gz) and correct the release notes, and keep address-level stores out of the public release until counsel clears the MSL clause. The B1 reader refuses this asset (hail.py:750-751 limits: 300 MiB and 20,000 files), which supports the rename.

findings.claim: The branch wait step may be unable to list the store job's runs, and its error handling turns a refused call into 'no store job', so the wait can silently do nothing. No test would catch it.
findings.evidence: The build job's permissions block (lines 48-50) grants contents: read and pages: read only. A job-level permissions block replaces the workflow-level one (lines 37-38, contents: read), so actions is none. Line 106 runs gh run list --workflow hail-store.yml --commit "$GITHUB_SHA" ... 2>/dev/null || echo "", and line 108 maps an empty result to 'no store job for this commit' and breaks. The repository is public (gh api reports visibility public), so I could not settle from here whether GitHub refuses this read with a token that has no actions scope. Either way the step cannot tell a refusal from no run. The test at tests/test_site.py:1831 only checks that the strings are present. Fix: add actions: read to the build job and fail the step when gh fails.

findings.claim: The wait comment says --require-live reports a stale asset after a timeout. It does not. A failed store job also lets the preview go on and read the previous asset, so a preview can pass on old data.
findings.evidence: Lines 103-104: 'If it runs longer, the build goes ahead and --require-live reports the stale asset.' build.py:257 records the hail source with ok=True on any successful load, whatever its as_of. build.py:675-676 fail only on sources whose ok is false. hail.py:375-376 sets out['stale'] for display and leaves ok unchanged. Line 109 (completed*) ... break) moves on after a 'completed failure' conclusion. So the preview reads whatever hail-store-b1.tar.gz exists: if a previous asset exists it passes, and if none exists the hail source fails. Fix: fail the wait on a non-success conclusion, have the preview compare the asset's as_of with the commit, and correct the comment.

findings.claim: The D34 amendment, the workflow comment (website.yml:126) and the test comment (tests/test_site.py:1838) say a failed store download reads 'Data unavailable'. The page does not say that.
findings.evidence: The page's failure words are 'Hail history is unavailable: {problem}. This is not the same as no hail.' (website/hail.py:163, WORDS['unavailable']). build.py:258-261 uses describe_unavailable for the town words, map.js:2433 fills h.words.unavailable, and docs/DESIGN.md:454 (the Unavailable row) gives the same words. Across website/, 'Data unavailable' appears only in map.js:2194 (storm reports). Fix the three statements, or change the words (next finding).

findings.claim: The hail failure words do not carry the phrase AGENTS.md rule 5 requires for missing inputs.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:82: 'Missing inputs show Data unavailable, never an all-clear.' hail.py:163: 'Hail history is unavailable: {problem}. This is not the same as no hail.' The wording is honest and is not an all-clear, so this is the owner's call: use the rule's phrase in WORDS['unavailable'] with a test, or record an exception in docs/DECISIONS.md.

findings.claim: The D34 amendment does not say which counsel gates are cleared for the flag now on main.
findings.evidence: Lines 733-735 keep the flag off until the owner approves the About text and counsel confirms the MSL clause 'for no other purpose', MCA 2-6-1017 and the GitHub Actions and Pages terms. Lines 741-742 say: 'The MSL clause and MCA 2-6-1017 concern the address stage (B3) and still gate that flag; the GitHub terms item stands as recorded.' Read as --hail-history, the gate still closes the flag on main. Read as the B3 flag, the record still does not say whether the GitHub terms item was confirmed, waived by the owner, or is open. The amendment also omits that the B1 gates are pending (DECISIONS.md:759; ROADMAP.md:38). Fix: for each item, say whether counsel confirmed it, the owner waived it (with the date), or it is open, and name the flag each one gates.

findings.claim: The B1 verification record still says 'Not ready to merge', and nothing records that its only blocking item is fixed.
findings.evidence: Line 8: 'Not ready to merge. BLOCKING: F1, the four compare-gate tests are skipped in CI because the website workflow installs no pyarrow ... Fix: add pyarrow to the install line at .github/workflows/website.yml:83.' HEAD's website.yml:90 installs pyarrow (git show HEAD), so F1 is fixed on this branch, and the discover run in this worktree reports no skips. ROADMAP.md:38 and DECISIONS.md:759 still say the gates are pending the re-check. Fix: update the verdict (F1 fixed by the commit that added pyarrow, B1-4 deferred to B2, F2 to F7 accepted or open) and cite it from the D34 amendment.

findings.claim: The B1 row's Limits cell still says the history is 'off on main until the owner approves the About text and counsel confirms the D34 items'.
findings.evidence: Line 38, Limits column: 'Radar estimates, not measurements or inspections; off on `main` until the owner approves the About text and counsel confirms the D34 items; ...'. The same row's first cell says '(merged 2026-10-21; public on `main`, the owner's decision)', and the heading at line 35 says 'B1 on `main` since 2026-10-21'. Fix: replace the 'off on main' clause with the current state and the open gates.

findings.claim: Two D34 sentences that this diff did not touch are now false: 'Built on claude/hail-b1, not merged.' (line 753) and 'The flag keeps the history off the public site until the owner has read the About text and counsel has read the terms.' (lines 763-764).
findings.evidence: The diff's only DECISIONS.md hunk is @@ -733,6 +733,13 @@, so lines 753 and 763-764 are unchanged. Fix: rewrite both in the present state.

findings.claim: The promise that a later stage's job 'never overwrites what main reads' is not enforced, and it has already failed once.
findings.evidence: The shared name was overwritten by a later stage's store on 2026-10-20T02:22:42Z (finding 1). Only the store job writes releases (hail-store.yml:76); the build job has contents: read (website.yml:49), so 'a branch preview' writes nothing, and the sentence should say 'store job'. A branch cut from main inherits the B1 name (hail-store.yml:66 and :76), and nothing checks that it is renamed before its first store-code push; tests/test_hail.py:1668-1669 pin only hail-store-b1.tar.gz. The same promise appears in README.md:94 and hail-store.yml:15-16. Fix: have branch store jobs publish under a branch-specific name or not to the public release, add a test for per-branch names, and correct the wording.

findings.claim: The design's Map status line ('Hail history didn't load at {time}: {detail}. This is not an all-clear.') does not exist in the code.
findings.evidence: A grep of website/ for 'Hail history didn't load' finds nothing. Other map features use 'didn't load' (map.js:205, 216, 2050). The code shows a hail failure through the sheet words (hail.py:163) and the source status line (build.py:260). Fix: align the design row with the code, or implement the sentence.

findings.claim: The header comment line is 171 characters, while the other comment lines are about 115, so the reflow is broken.
findings.evidence: awk 'length > 120' flags hail-store.yml line 5 at 171 characters. The line joins the B1 sentence and the 12:43 sentence without a break.

findings.claim: The step name capitalises 'Hail' mid-sentence, unlike the sentence case used elsewhere.
findings.evidence: Step name: 'Wait for this commit's Hail history store job (branch pushes; the preview reads the asset it publishes)'. Running text in the docs uses 'the hail history' (About: 'The hail history is NOAA's radar estimate').

findings.claim: 'the daily job takes about 12' and 'usually within the hour' are unmeasured timing claims.
findings.evidence: docs/ROADMAP.md:40 says the daily job's run time is pending the re-check. The 'usually within the hour' claim also appears in website/templates/about.html:41, website/hail.py:166 and website/sources.py:200. Fix: measure on the first runs and cite it, or soften the wording.

findings.claim: Statements that the flag is on main 'since' or 'merged' 2026-10-21 are written before the merge.
findings.evidence: The date is written as past in README.md:7, :57 and :94; AGENTS.md:50; docs/ROADMAP.md:35 and :38; docs/DECISIONS.md:736; .github/workflows/website.yml:125; and .github/workflows/hail-store.yml:5. These are true only if the merge happens on 2026-10-21. Set the date at merge time.

findings.claim: The original 'Off on main (7)' bullet still reads as current above its amendment.
findings.evidence: Lines 733-735: '--hail-history is off by default ... It stays off until Carson says the About text is right ...', followed by the amendment at line 736. Mark the original as superseded, or rewrite the bullet.

findings.claim: The timeout assertion would pass on any 'timeout-minutes: 60', and it does not tie the build job's timeout to the 40-minute wait cap. The wait's error path is untested.
findings.evidence: tests/test_site.py:1847 is self.assertIn('timeout-minutes: 60', text). The wait cap is 40 checks of 60 seconds (website.yml:105-112), and nothing in the docs times the build steps that run after the wait. No test covers the gh error path (website.yml:106-108).

findings.claim: On the merge push, the public site will show 'Hail history is unavailable' until the first main store job publishes hail-store-b1.tar.gz.
findings.evidence: The release lists only hail-store.tar.gz (gh api assets). Line 127 adds --hail-history on main, and hail-store.yml's push trigger includes website/hail.py (lines 17-21). The store job and the main build therefore both start on the merge push, and the build cannot wait for the job. This is the designed fallback (hail.py:163; website.yml:125-126), but the go-live note should say so.

result.notes:
Method: I read the full diff (9 files), both workflows in full, about.html, the hail WORDS and fetch path (hail.py, build.py, sources.py), the D34, ROADMAP, README and AGENTS hunks, DESIGN.md section 9, and the B1 verification record. Live reads were read-only (gh api, and one curl of the public asset). git status in the worktree was identical before and after every run.

Tests, quoted tails. (1) The lens command as written (python -m unittest tests.test_site -k workflow tests.test_hail -k daily_job -k constants) exits 2 with 'python -m unittest: error: unrecognized arguments: tests.test_hail'. Nearest valid runs: -k workflow tests.test_site gives 'Ran 1 test in 10.553s ... OK'; -k daily_job -k constants tests.test_hail gives 'Ran 2 tests in 0.000s ... OK' (test_constants_and_names and test_the_daily_job_installs_unpinned_like_the_site_build). (2) The workflow's own unit step (website.yml:94, same modules): 'Ran 548 tests in 109.505s ... OK', exit 0, no skips. (3) AGENTS.md's required command, python -m unittest discover -s tests: 'Ran 592 tests in 112.821s ... OK', exit 0, no skipped lines. All runs used Python 3.13.16 from the venv; the workflow pins 3.12, which I did not run. I did not run python desktop/launcher.py --selftest payload, since the diff does not touch payload/ or desktop/.

Asset name: hail.py:92 (STORE_URL), hail-store.yml:66 (tar) and :76 (upload) all say hail-store-b1.tar.gz, and tests/test_hail.py:824 and :1668-1669 pin them.

Words: no em dash, en dash, or model, vendor or AI-product names in the 59 added lines. New headings are sentence case.

About text: every sentence of the hail section and of WORDS states a radar estimate. The word rule (hail.py:23) holds: WORDS contains no damage, dry, clear, insurance, eligible or confirmed, and 'no hail' appears only negated. The 0.25 in floor matches the code (hail.py:66 FLOOR_TENTHS = 64; hail.py:906 np.rint). The wording problems are the failure words only (findings 4 and 5).

Checks that hold: the rename is needed, because the public asset exceeds B1's reader limits (hail.py:750-751: 300 MiB and 20,000 files; the asset has 31,129 files and 357.3 MiB). B1's own build is 4,597 files and 31,287,983 bytes (round-1 measurement in the B1 record), inside those limits. Download failures: Fetcher.binary has a 20 s per-request timeout, three attempts and no size cap (sources.py:686, 724-742); tar and gzip errors map to HailStoreError (hail.py:669-703); build.py:258 catches the errors that reach it. I found no escape path that would stop the main build, and main has no --require-live (website.yml:127).

Not verified: GitHub's answer to the wait's gh call on this token (finding 2); the timing claims (finding 14); gate results beyond what the record states.

Scratch: /home/user/hail-b1/out/review-live/reviewer/ holds the logs, inspect_store.py and asset/hail-store.tar.gz. The archive was listed and read for key names only. It was never extracted, and no values were printed.
